body.target_estimand: The published target \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) and the component-aligned target \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\) are coefficient projections of \(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\) and \(\mathfrak F_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\), respectively, with numerical duplicates removed. On maintained inputs, \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\) identifies the first with \(\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}\), while \(\texttt{thm:component-aligned-fiber-projection-exactness}\) identifies the second with the \(T_\pi\) indexed by source-to-sink paths of \(\mathcal D_G^{\mathrm{live}}\).
body.estimand_functional: On \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), \(\operatorname{Enum}_G(\mathcal O_G)=\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) and \(\mathcal A_G(\mathcal O_G)=\varnothing\). On \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\), \(\operatorname{Enum}_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)=\Theta_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\) and the same q-pruned pass computes \(\mathcal A_G^{\mathrm{CA}}(\mathcal O_G)\), with total ordered-exact-real time \(O((m+|E|)p^3 2^p+p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}+mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}})\) and polynomial-envelope space.

sampling_model.design: The population input is the exact collection of within-view covariance blocks and cross-view blocks observed on an arbitrary fixed graph \(G\). The published mode uses only marginal regressions because edge residuals are unrestricted nuisance. The component-aligned mode additionally computes edgewise Schur states and \(q\)-scores, constructs the full \(2^p\) compatibility DAG, and prunes it from source to sink.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment. The structural targets are the coefficient projections of the published and component-aligned mechanism fibers and the ancestry relations common to their union-support DAGs.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The published layer assumes centered finite-second-moment product disturbances within each view, positive within-view variances, and a shared order, while allowing arbitrary cross-view disturbance covariance. The pairing-informative layer additionally assumes cross-coordinate component alignment and positive-definite coordinate-stack covariance.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All new results are exact population identification and enumeration statements. Sampling uncertainty is inherited only through the parent's covariance-region inversion; no new estimator rate, limit law, polynomial enumeration of a continuum region, or substitution of a point enumerator for region inversion is claimed.

The present all-orders theorem gives the unrestricted covariance boundary, and the component-aligned fiber and q-path theorems give the separately qualified pairing-informative result.

Theorem 7 gives the chordal positive-definite completion boundary. Here maintained component-aligned inputs obtain coordinate completions from principal blocks of a full residual covariance; no polynomial off-model nonchordal completion algorithm is claimed.
Theorem 3 partitions represented DAGs by distinct total-effect functionals, motivating output quotienting but not covariance-dependent coefficient-row fragments.
Theorems 1, 4, and 5 and Corollary 1 enumerate graph-distinct acyclic orientations or consistent extensions; they do not collapse orders sharing one numerical coefficient tuple.
The paper gives polynomial-delay quotient enumeration for local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph. The present right congruences are proved from immutable numerical row projections.
Theorem 7 supplies output-dependent delay for a projected star query, providing generic projection-enumeration context but no LiMVAM coefficient theorem.
Reverse search is generic exact-enumeration context based on a locally computable parent relation; it does not provide the numerical fragment congruence used here.
The survey supplies generic output-sensitive subgraph-enumeration context and terminology, not the LiMVAM immutable-row quotient theorem.
Colored Gaussian DAG algebra is adjacent to covariance-constrained structural models but does not establish the transformed-covariance all-orders witness or fragment enumerator here.
DirectLiNGAM supplies recursive-residual causal-discovery ancestry; it does not prove the multi-view q-path fiber characterization or exact-once component-aligned tuple quotient.
The CamCAN repository motivates the multi-view MEG and MRI application setting but supplies no identification or enumeration theorem.

Fraction-free elimination controls exact divisibility and minor growth for each rational solve; the present theorems add simultaneous output-polynomial accounting over subset regressions, q-states, row certificates, fragments, outputs, and ancestry tests.

body.tldr: The observed covariance law supports two exact but different conclusions. Under the published shared-order LiMVAM primitives, unrestricted cross-view disturbance dependence makes every order covariance-compatible and makes common union-support ancestry empty, so pairing contributes neither pruning nor ancestry. Under the component-aligned subclass, the independently defined mechanism fiber is exactly represented by source-to-sink paths of the live \(q\)-DAG. A two-mode immutable-row dynamic program emits each distinct coefficient tuple once; its pairing-informative component-aligned mode runs in \(O((m+|E|)p^3 2^p+p^3 2^pN_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}}+mp^2N_{\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{CA}})\) ordered exact-real time and computes the nontrivial subclass ancestry intersection. For rational inputs, both modes have deterministic subset-exponential, output-sensitive total bit bounds polynomial in the listed parameters including explicit \(2^p\); these are not output-polynomial guarantees in the conventional input-plus-output sense.

project_justification.gap: The parent calibration frontier had a \(2^p\)-state compatibility recursion but no noncircular exact-once enumeration of distinct numerical coefficient tuples. The previous repair correctly exposed the unrestricted-cross-view all-orders boundary but left the pairing-informative component-aligned coefficient target as an observable order refinement rather than an independent mechanism projection.
project_justification.niche: The note separates the published mechanism fiber from its component-aligned subclass fiber. Within-view normal equations uniquely map any fiber mechanism and order to its immutable modified-Cholesky rows. The published fiber projects onto all orders, whereas the component-aligned fiber projects exactly onto live \(q\)-DAG paths by residual factorization and positive-definite coordinate completion.
project_justification.fill: Source-to-sink pruning makes every retained prefix extendable. Equal immutable original-label fragments at a fixed removed set have identical suffix outputs, unequal fragments have disjoint completion sets, and each bucket charges to at most the final numerical output count. Exact row sorting and integer tries therefore yield exact-once full-lattice and q-pruned enumerators without a real hash oracle or factorial order traversal.

body.technical_internal_limitation: The guarantees are total output-sensitive bounds over an explicit \(2^p\) state space, not polynomial delay, not polynomial time in \(p\), and not output-polynomial in the conventional input-plus-output sense. Ordered exact-real arithmetic is not a floating-point stability guarantee; for rational inputs the bit theorems instead control certificate height and total bit cost as polynomials in parameter lists that explicitly include \(2^p\). The \(q\)-DAG theorem requires maintained component-aligned inputs and does not provide polynomial preprocessing for arbitrary off-model nonchordal partial covariances. Gaussianity is used only to construct existential completion witnesses, not assumed of the generating law. The results enumerate exact population coefficient sets, not continuum-valued covariance-region inverses.
body.honest_scope: The published shared-order class retains arbitrary cross-view disturbance covariance: pairing supplies neither order pruning nor common ancestry there, although the full-lattice algorithm still removes numerical duplicates without enumerating permutations. The pairing-informative result is exactly the component-aligned subclass with positive-definite coordinate covariance blocks, on an arbitrary observed view graph and at model-generated population moments. It proves \(q\)-path/fiber equivalence, exact-once tuple enumeration, nontrivial ancestry post-processing, ordered-exact-real complexity, and deterministic rational subset-exponential, output-sensitive total bit complexity with explicit \(2^p\) dependence. It does not claim unrestricted LiMVAM identification, conventional output-polynomial complexity, polynomial delay, off-model nonchordal completion, floating-point robustness, or finite enumeration of the parent's covariance-region inverse.
body.interpretation: Unrestricted cross-view pairing is causally uninformative at the covariance level in this model: every order has a Gaussian covariance witness, and choosing the reverse order for any pair proves that published common ancestry is empty. Component alignment changes the conclusion. Its observed edge blocks prune the order set through the live \(q\)-DAG, and the exact-once stream yields a potentially nonempty common ancestry intersection. Numerical fragment merging can be substantial in both modes because many structural orders may induce the same coefficient tuple.
